title: the Glass Steppe Rising Revisited
premise: Felix Brightwater, a temple scribe bound by debt to the silent gods of the valley, discovers that the old deities have begun answering prayers again — and that his own blood is the ink they write with. When a dragon-keeper named Sera Ashfall arrives hunting the last living dragon-fire, Felix must choose between the duty that owns him and the stranger who sees him truly. Together they carry a secret: the valley's magiclessness is not a curse but a cage, built to imprison a god whose waking would reignite the ancient war between dragons and divinity. In the end, Felix breaks his debt by breaking the valley's silence, sacrificing his own name to memory so the god sleeps on and dragon-fire survives — while Sera carries their story out into a world that will finally remember him.
about_author: J. M. Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing abandoned manuscripts before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people trapped by obligations they never chose.

chapters.title: Ink That Will Not Dry
chapters.summary: Felix Brightwater copies prayers in the Temple of Quiet Hours, where no prayer has ever been answered. When one of his transcriptions begins rewriting itself overnight, he hides it, terrified of what debt-collectors or priests would do. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath a life of numbing routine.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Knocked Twice
chapters.summary: Sera Ashfall arrives in the valley seeking the source of a dying flame she has tracked for years, but the valley swallows her magic at its border. She hires Felix as a guide because he can read the old script; he agrees to pay down his debt. POV: alternating Felix and Sera. Emotional beat: wary attraction between two people who distrust being needed.

chapters.title: What the Valley Forgot
chapters.summary: Following the self-writing prayer into the hills, they find ruins that predate the temple — and a stone door that hums with heat in a land where fire cannot live. Sera realizes the valley isn't dead; it's sealed. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into fear as she understands what's buried here.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector's Ledger
chapters.summary: The temple's high priest reveals Felix's debt was never money: his family sold his name generations ago to keep the seal fed. The self-writing prayers are the imprisoned god testing its chains through him. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: betrayal — his whole identity was collateral.

chapters.title: Ashes Answer
chapters.summary: Sera confesses her true errand: the last dragon is dying, and only god-fire can rekindle its line. She asks Felix to open the door, not knowing it would free a war-god. Their argument becomes something closer to a vow. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: love declared in the shape of an impossible request.

chapters.title: The God Beneath the Steppe
chapters.summary: They descend beneath the glass flats and meet the imprisoned god, who offers Felix a bargain: freedom from his debt in exchange for carrying its secret back to the world. Felix glimpses the ancient war and understands why the valley was made. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: temptation — everything he wants, at everyone else's cost.

chapters.title: Prayers With Teeth
chapters.summary: The god's whispers spread through the valley; answered prayers begin exacting prices, and villagers turn on the temple. The high priest moves to erase Felix's name entirely and reseal the door with a fresh sacrifice. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: panic and resolve as survival demands he stop running.

chapters.title: The Guttering Flame
chapters.summary: Sera races to the last dragon, who lies dying at the valley's edge, and learns the truth she fled: dragon-fire was the original chain, willingly given. Rekindling it means asking the dragon to burn again as a prisoner. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: grief for a cause that was never clean.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: At the stone door, priest, god, and lovers collide. Felix chooses neither side: he offers his own name — his memories, his selfhood — as new ink for the seal, sparing the dragon and starving the god. Sera holds him as he forgets himself line by line. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: climax — love against duty resolved by paying both prices at once.

chapters.title: Rising, Remembered
chapters.summary: The valley opens; magic returns gently; the dragon-fire kindles anew under Sera's care. She finds Felix alive but unnamed, tending the temple garden, and begins telling him their story every evening — writing him back into existence. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: bittersweet hope; identity rebuilt by love, one retelling at a time.
